annotations.text:
AS SHIPPED — the baseline.
Five blocks on five unrelated baselines: the left stack starts at grid-row 3 and the right at row 2, and both centre their contents in tracks of different heights, so their tops can never relate.

01 · FOOTER TRANSPORT — PICKED, and now shipped.
The axis is the stage's THIRD RAIL: the two vertical HUD rails carry space, this one carries time. It meets them at their own feet, and the projector's contact plane sits on it — Vince stands on the year.
Scope left, facts right. Loadout dropped. The rule runs rail to rail; the stops are inset so the first and last year clear the brandmark and the control cluster.

02 · THE SHOULDERS — your own proposal, literally.
Switcher: previous era bottom-left, next bottom-right, six ticks between them for position.
Panels: one continuous spine per column, each section a tick stepping off it. No head rules at all.
Trade-off: ±1 era per click — a scrub, not an index.

03 · THE INDEX COLUMN — the Cyberpunk codex read.
Switcher: a six-row list owning the left column, gold left bearing on the active row.
Panels: everything consolidates right as one ruled register; the title moves INTO it, so a list on the left and a title on the right can never be confused.
Trade-off: three columns of unequal weight; the most application-like of the seven.

04 · THE DATED SPINE — draw the record, not a tab strip.
Switcher: a real dated axis, 2014–2026, eras at their true dates so the GAPS are part of the reading.
Panels: a graduation ladder on each outboard edge; heads carry a long gold tick instead of an underline.
Trade-off: most house-consistent, least character-select.

05 · THE CONSOLE — reopens the “no boxes” ruling, deliberately.
ONE machined housing on the right (TR+BL chamfer, gold hairline, square children) with the era tabs fused inside its top edge, so they read as that panel's control rather than page navigation. Left stays bare.
Trade-off: you closed this in August. Included so the choice is explicit — if boxes are still out, this is the option that proves it.

06 · THE CARTRIDGE DECK — eras as objects, not words.
Switcher: six chamfered plates on the floor, year + glyph, the active one raised and lit. No era name in the deck at all, so duplication is impossible by construction.
Panels: ADR-065 brackets — framed, not a device, so the cartridges stay the only chamfered things on screen.
Trade-off: six glyphs is real work, and this is the one most at risk of reading as game chrome.

07 · THE RIGHT LADDER — maximum distance from the title.
Switcher: a vertical year ladder set into the right HUD rail, where the bearing/sector readouts live (they step aside for it).
Panels: a flat recess wash — material without a container, no border, no rule.
Trade-off: a wash IS a fill, so this is the closest of the six non-box options to what you rejected; and the recess must be re-measured in light, where the ground inverts.
